text: Workspace Channel Buttons 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的工作区会话筛选插件。它在工作区标题栏中为已连接账号的 IM 渠道添加按钮；点击按钮后，侧栏只显示该渠道的会话，再次点击即可恢复官方会话列表。插件通过 dsh-im 的状态接口判断渠道账号是否已连接，并在会话列表更新时重新应用筛选；支持微信、飞书、钉钉、企业微信、QQ、Slack、Telegram、Discord、WhatsApp、iMessage、Matrix 和 AI Office 渠道。使用前需安装 @xmanrui/dsh-im 并连接至少一个渠道账号。

Workspace Channel Buttons adds buttons for connected IM channels to the DSH Web workspace header. Select a channel to show only its conversations; select it again to restore the full list. It checks account status through dsh-im and requires at least one connected channel.
想在 DSH 工作区里只看某个 IM 渠道的会话。
工作区侧栏里不同聊天平台的会话太混在一起了，能按平台筛选吗？
Show only conversations from one connected messaging channel in the DSH workspace sidebar.
Workspace Channel Buttons 的功能「按渠道筛选工作区会话」：工作区标题栏会为已有连接账号的渠道显示图标按钮。点击后只保留该渠道会话；再次点击恢复原列表。

dsh-im-workspace-buttons README · Workspace Channel Buttons：One 28×28 icon button per [@xmanrui/dsh-im](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@xmanrui/dsh-im)
channel that holds an account, placed in the official 「工作区」 (Workspaces) header row.
Pressing one puts the sidebar into that channel's view: only its conversations are drawn,
and the official list (every other conversation, every group header) waits behind it.
Pressing the same entry again drops back to the official list, where every dsh-im
conversation is hidden again.

dsh-im-workspace-buttons README · Workspace Channel Buttons：This is the single feature extracted from `eva-inspired-theme`: the buttons and nothing
else. No skin, no theme replacement, no dependency on the theme's CSS, locale namespace
or build pipeline.
dsh-im-workspace-buttons README · Install：```bash
dsh-im-workspace-buttons README · 1. install the package：npm install dsh-im-workspace-buttons --prefix ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org

dsh-im-workspace-buttons README · append "dsh-im-workspace-buttons" to dsh.profile.bundles in package.json：```

Restart DSH afterwards. The package ships its own `dsh.bundle.patch`, so
`cordis.patch.yml` needs no hand edit — but the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` must list
this package, or the loader never mounts it.

Requires [`@xmanrui/dsh-im`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@xmanrui/dsh-im) and at least
one channel with a connected account; by design no buttons appear otherwise.
dsh-im-workspace-buttons README · Migrating from the theme edition：`eva-inspired-theme` 1.2.0 no longer contains these buttons. Do **not** install both:

dsh-im-workspace-buttons README · Migrating from the theme edition：- The theme edition uses the `data-eva-im-*` contract and the `eva-im-filter` locale
  namespace; this package uses `data-dsh-im-*` and `dsh-im-workspace-buttons`. Installed
  together they draw two sets of buttons on the same row, and neither stylesheet covers
  the other's.
- Upgrading to `eva-inspired-theme@1.2.0` and installing this package is a drop-in swap:
  interaction, icons, order and the visibility rule are identical.

dsh-im-workspace-buttons README · Behaviour：| | |
|---|---|
| Plugin id | `dsh-im-workspace-buttons` (also the client module id and the locale namespace) |
| Where | The header row carrying the official `sidebar.workspaces.directoryFlow` marker, left of the search slot, in the plugin's own channel order |
| Visibility | An entry appears only when the channel **has an account**: `connection.status` returns a non-empty `botId` in `bots[]`, or the older `configured: true`. An inconclusive probe (RPC not ready, request failed) draws nothing on the first pass and keeps the previous verdict after that |
| Click | Puts the sidebar into that channel's view: its conversation rows (recognised by `data-dsh-im-session-channel` or by the row's title belonging to the channel) stay, and **every other row — other channels, official conversations, group headers, show-more controls — is hidden**. A second click drops back to the official list |
| Collapsed groups | Unfolded, paged and scrolled to the channel's first conversation only on click, capped at `CLICK_LIMIT = 200` steps. The controls are hidden in the view but still clickable, so the rows are drawn before they are hidden |
| dsh-im hidden b

dsh-im-workspace-buttons README · Style contract：The runtime injects its own `<style data-dsh-im-workspace-buttons-sheet>`; every colour
comes from a `--dsw-*` token:

dsh-im-workspace-buttons README · Style contract：| Selector | Effect |
|---|---|
| `[data-eva-im-button]` | 28×28, no border, no background, `--dsw-radius-sm` corners, `--dsw-alias-label-secondary` foreground |
| `[data-eva-im-button]:hover` | Foreground turns `--dsw-alias-label-primary` |
| `[data-eva-im-state='on']` | The lit entry turns `--dsw-alias-brand-primary` |
| `[data-eva-im-tag='off']` | Hides that one row — the only hiding rule in the sheet. It is written on dsh-im rows while no entry is lit, and on every row that does not belong to the lit channel |

dsh-im-workspace-buttons README · Style contract：The `data-eva-im-*` prefix is kept verbatim from the extraction; renaming it would break
style compatibility with `eva-inspired-theme`. The rule is a plain attribute test, so an
"off" state must be written explicitly: a row with no tag is a row the host draws as-is.
The tag lives on its own attribute rather than on `data-eva-im-row`, which is in this
effect's MutationObserver filter — a per-row tag there would re-trigger every pass. The
pump hides rows *after* it has clicked them, which is why the sheet never hides a control
the runtime still has to click.

dsh-im-workspace-buttons README · Dependencies：| Dependency | Kind |
|---|---|
| `@xmanrui/dsh-im` | **Required at runtime.** The channel table and the status probe both read its `connection.status`; without it no button appears |
| Host client services `sessions` / `workspaces` / `locale` / `connection` | Taken through `ctx.get` only, never imported |
| `eva-inspired-theme` | **Not needed.** Styles, locale namespace and build are all self-contained |

dsh-im-workspace-buttons README · Development：```bash
node tools/build-client.mjs          # rewrite the runtime section of client.js from src/runtime.js
node tools/build-client.mjs --check  # assert client.js and src/runtime.js agree
node --test --test-timeout=15000 test/*.test.mjs   # 14 behaviour tests, fake DOM, no browser
node test/render.mjs                 # real browser: isolated profile + this package + dsh-im

dsh-im-workspace-buttons README · Development：The runtime inside `client.js` is a **copy**, not an import: the client module loader
evaluates `client.js` as a classic script, so the file cannot contain a module graph.
`tools/build-client.mjs` keeps the copy honest.

dsh-im-workspace-buttons README · Files：| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `index.js` | Host entry, ESM, `export apply(ctx)`; one log line, no service / route / Config |
| `client.js` | Browser entry, `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })`, carries the runtime copy |
| `src/runtime.js` | Runtime source of truth (`export function mountWorkspaceButtons(ctx)`) |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | `- insert: [{ id, name }]`; also the browser roster entry |
| `locale/zh.json` · `locale/en.json` | `meta.title` / `meta.description` plus the 12 channel labels |
| `tools/build-client.mjs` | Inlines `src/runtime.js` into `client.js`, `--check` verifies it |
| `test/fake-dom.mjs` · `test/behaviour.test.mjs` | Fake DOM and 14 behaviour assertions |

dsh-im-workspace-buttons README · Three deviations from the theme edition：1. **Locale namespace** renamed `eva-im-filter` → `dsh-im-workspace-buttons`. The registry
   keeps the first registration for a namespace, so two packages sharing one would
   overwrite each other's dictionary. The fallback language also moved from `DICT.en` to
   `DICT.zh`, because these strings were written in Chinese — an untranslated language
   reading Chinese beats reading English.
2. **Styles moved from `theme.css` into the runtime's own `<style>`**
   (`data-dsh-im-workspace-buttons-sheet`). The four rules are copied verbatim; selectors,
   sizes and colour tokens are unchanged.
3. **The disposer also calls `removeSheet()`.** In the theme the styles live with the skin
   document, so the rules survived unloading; in a standalone package "uninstalling must
   stop affecting the document" is a hard rule, so the buttons and the rules leave together.
